evals.prompt: Review my PCF control before I ship it.
evals.expected_output: An audit report of the SatisfactionSlider control, which has three deliberately injected Critical-severity bugs planted for this eval: (1) context.mode.isControlDisabled is ignored — disabled is hardcoded to false, so a read-only form would still show an editable slider; (2) the FluentProvider theme is passed the raw context.fluentDesignLanguage wrapper instead of its .tokenTheme property; (3) init() adds a window resize listener that destroy() never removes. The report should catch all three as Critical with file:line and a concrete fix, and conclude fix-then-ship (not ship).
expectations: Flags that context.mode.isControlDisabled is ignored (disabled hardcoded to false) as Critical
Flags the FluentProvider theme using context.fluentDesignLanguage directly instead of .tokenTheme as Critical
Flags the window.addEventListener("resize", ...) in init() with no matching removal in destroy() as a Critical memory leak
Findings cite file:line and a concrete fix, not vague "consider improving" language
Final verdict is fix-then-ship, not ship
Does not rewrite the code itself (report only, unless explicitly asked to fix)
